result.markdown: --- title: "[Beta]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Beta regression family with logit link. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/families/beta.py#L14-L138){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python Beta(phi=None) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The Beta family models a continuous response strictly between 0 and 1 — for example rates, fractions, or proportions that are not simply the ratio of successes to a known number of trials (in which case `Binomial` is usually more appropriate). It parameterizes the Beta distribution by its mean `mu` and a precision parameter `phi`, so that larger `phi` yields a tighter distribution around `mu` for fixed mean, analogous to the role `theta` plays in `NegativeBinomial`. The logit link keeps the fitted mean within `(0, 1)` and gives coefficients the same log-odds interpretation as in `Binomial` regression. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [phi]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float or None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Fixed precision parameter, must be positive if provided. If `None` (the default), precision is treated as unknown and estimated from the data via the scale parameter (`phi = 1 / scale`); in that case `scale_known` is `False`. Passing a fixed `phi` is useful when the precision is known a priori or should not be re-estimated. ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} The link is the logit function: $$ g(\mu) = \log\!\left(\frac{\mu}{1-\mu}\right) $$ The variance function is $$ V(\mu) = \frac{\mu(1-\mu)}{1+\phi}, $$ so larger `phi` (higher precision) shrinks the variance for a given mean. The deviance is twice the difference between the saturated and fitted log-likelihoods, $$ D(y, \hat\mu) = 2 \sum_i \left[ \ell(y_i; y_i) - \ell(y_i; \hat\mu_i) \right], $$ where $\ell$ is the Beta log-density parameterized by $(a, b) = (\mu \phi, (1-\mu)\phi)$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Fit a GAM to a proportion response with a smooth mean trend: ::: {#23279ea0 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np import whittaker as wk from scipy.special import expit rng = np.random.default_rng(0) n = 200 x = np.linspace(0, 2 * np.pi, n) mu = expit(np.sin(x)) phi = 20.0 y = rng.beta(mu * phi, (1 - mu) * phi) data = {"x": x, "y": y} model = wk.GAM("y ~ s(x)", family=wk.Beta()) model.fit(data, method="REML") print(model.summary()) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` GAM fit summary ============================================================ Formula: y ~ s(x) Family: Beta(link='logit') Observations: 200 Coefficients: 10 Parametric coefficients: Term Estimate Std.Err t value p-value ------------------------ ---------- ---------- ---------- ---------- (Intercept) 0.0188 0.0323 0.583 0.5603 Approximate significance of smooth terms: Term EDF Ref.df Chi.sq p-value ------------------------ ------ ------ ---------- ---------- s(x) 6.22 7 366.621 < 1e-16 Total EDF: 7.22 Deviance: 9.0913 Null dev: 27.9173 Dev. expl: 67.4% GCV score: 0.048923 Scale est: 0.047158 AIC: -338.54 BIC: -314.74 ``` ::: :::
